# SFTP

<!-- BEGIN generated by .github/scripts/plugin_pages.py from the package's describe.json -->

SFTP servers: the `sftp` destination, from the `sftp` package. Declare the package once in `dependencies.yml`; DRE installs it on demand:

```yaml
# dependencies.yml
plugins:
  - sftp
```

### Profile fields

Set in `profiles.yml`, under `destinations:`, in a target with `type: sftp`.

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `host` (required) |  | SFTP server. |
| `port` | `22` | Port. |
| `username` (required) |  | User name. |
| `accept_unknown_host` |  | Trust a host missing from known_hosts. |
| `password` |  | Password (or set private_key_path) Secret: use `env_var()`. |
| `private_key_path` |  | Private key file (instead of a password) A file path; `~/` is your home directory. |
| `private_key_passphrase` |  | The private key's passphrase. Secret: use `env_var()`. |
| `known_hosts_path` |  | Known_hosts file (default ~/.ssh/known_hosts) A file path; `~/` is your home directory. |
| `private_key` |  | The private key's text, e.g. from env_var() (instead of private_key_path) Secret: use `env_var()`. |
| `host_key_fingerprint` |  | Pinned host key, SHA256:... (otherwise ~/.ssh/known_hosts is used) |
| `use_agent` |  | Sign in with the keys in your SSH agent (SSH_AUTH_SOCK), instead of a password or key file. |
| `allow_rsa_keys` |  | False refuses RSA private keys; true uses them without the RUSTSEC-2023-0071 warning. |
| `connect_timeout` | `30s` | How long to wait for a connection (`30s`, `2m`, or seconds) A duration (`30s`, `2m`) or seconds. |
| `timeout` | `60s` | How long a read or write may make no progress before it fails. A duration (`30s`, `2m`) or seconds. |
| `retries` | `3` | How many times to try again after a temporary error (0: never) |

### Options

Set in the report's `output.destination` entry.

| Option | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `if_exists` | string | `overwrite` | When a file is already at the path: `overwrite` it, fail with `error`, or `number` the new one. One of `overwrite`, `error`, `number`. |
| `atomic` | boolean | `true` | Upload under a temporary name, then rename, so no half-written file appears. |
| `temp_dir` | string |  | Where the temporary file goes (on the same server), for receivers that pick up any new file. |

<!-- END generated -->

## Notes

`host`, `port` (22), `username`, and `password`, `private_key_path` or `private_key`
(+ `private_key_passphrase`). `private_key` is the key's text, for when it can't be a file (a CI
secret: `private_key: "{{ env_var('SFTP_KEY') }}"`); a key stored on one line with literal `\n`
gets its line breaks back. Set `private_key_path` or `private_key`, not both. The host key is
checked against `known_hosts_path` (default `~/.ssh/known_hosts`) or a pinned
`host_key_fingerprint` (`SHA256:...`). In `private_key_path` and `known_hosts_path`, a leading
`~/` is your home directory. Unknown hosts are refused unless `accept_unknown_host` is true.
With `use_agent` set to `true`, it signs in with the keys in your SSH agent (`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`; the OpenSSH agent's
pipe on Windows) instead of a password or key file, so the key never enters DRE.
Missing directories are created. Uploads go under a temporary name first (`atomic`, `temp_dir`:
see [Uploads under a temporary name](plugins.md#uploads-under-a-temporary-name)); `if_exists` is checked in the same step as the
write (see [A file already at the path](plugins.md#a-file-already-at-the-path)). The [`postgres`](plugin-postgres.md)
source's `ssh:` block takes the same settings.

## RSA keys

RSA private keys sign through the `rsa` crate, which has a known timing weakness
([RUSTSEC-2023-0071](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html)) and no fixed
release yet. This applies to `sftp` and to the `postgres` source's `ssh:` tunnel, and only to
RSA keys DRE reads itself (`private_key_path`, `private_key`). Ed25519 and ECDSA keys, passwords
and `use_agent: true` don't use it.

The practical risk is low: an attack needs precise timings of many signatures, and DRE signs once
per connection, a few times a run. So DRE keeps RSA keys working and warns once per run.
`allow_rsa_keys` changes that:

| Value | What happens |
|---|---|
| unset | RSA keys work, with a warning naming the advisory. |
| `true` | RSA keys work without the warning: you've read this, and the key is only for a server you trust (a bank's SFTP server that accepts nothing else, say). |
| `false` | RSA keys are refused, with what to do instead: for teams that want them blocked. |

To move off RSA: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, add the `.pub` file on the server
(its `authorized_keys`, or the bank's key upload), and point `private_key_path` at the new key.
Or keep the RSA key in your SSH agent and set `use_agent: true`: OpenSSH signs, not DRE.

## Deliver a file without exposing a partial upload

Use the complete [SFTP delivery example](https://github.com/get-dre/dre/blob/master/examples/sftp-delivery/) for a runnable local server
and report. For a real receiving server, use its verified host key and a key file:

```yaml
# profiles.yml
destinations:
  partner:
    targets:
      dev: {deliver: false}
      prod:
        type: sftp
        host: sftp.example.com
        username: reporting
        private_key_path: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
        known_hosts_path: ~/.ssh/known_hosts
```

```yaml
# within a report's output
destination:
  profile: partner
  path: "incoming/report-{{ run.date.yyyymmdd }}.csv"
  atomic: true
  temp_dir: staging
  if_exists: error
```

`temp_dir` and the final path must allow a rename on the same server. The receiving system
should watch `incoming`, not `staging`. `sftp/host-key-mismatch` requires verifying the server
identity with its administrator before updating the pin; disabling the check hides a changed
server. `sftp/file-exists` needs a new dated name or a deliberate replacement policy.
See [atomic upload behavior](plugins.md#uploads-under-a-temporary-name),
[destination keys](reference-report.md#outputdestination) and [destination](glossary.md#destination).
